title: High-Valence Nickel Single-Atom Catalysts Coordinated to Oxygen Sites for Extraordinarily Activating Oxygen Evolution Reaction
text: NaCl template synthesis was used to prepare nickel single-atom catalysts coordinated to oxygen sites on graphene-like carbon, denoted Ni-O-G SACs. Nickel chloride and sucrose were dissolved in NaCl solution, freeze-dried, annealed at 700 C under argon, and then NaCl was removed. The resulting Ni-O-G SACs showed a 3D porous framework made of ultrathin graphene-like sheets. XRD showed graphene framework peaks without Ni metal or oxide nanoparticles. BET showed a specific surface area of 580 m2 g-1. HAADF-STEM revealed atomically dispersed Ni atoms. XPS and XANES showed high-valence Ni species higher than Ni(II). EXAFS fitting indicated a Ni-O4(OH)2-like oxygen-saturated coordination environment. For OER in 1 m KOH, Ni-O-G SACs required an overpotential of 224 mV to reach 10 mA cm-2, with a Tafel slope of 42 mV dec-1. The oxygen production turnover frequency reached 1.44 s-1 at 300 mV and 2.81 s-1 at 350 mV. Chronoamperometry at 400 mV showed a stable current density of 115 mA cm-2 for 50 h without significant degradation. Compared with NiO, bulk Ni-O-G, Ni-N-G SACs, O-G, and RuO2, Ni-O-G SACs showed the best activity. DFT calculations suggested that bonding between single Ni atoms and oxygen sites strongly promoted OER activity and durability.
